comment: The observation that shared components serve many programmes at once and that pooling investment across them is therefore efficient matches Slovenia's experience. We would add a practical qualification: pooling is easier to sustain where the shared components are procured and governed as one programme with a single accountable authority. Slovenia is building several foundational components under one co-financed national programme with the National Institute of Public Health as steward, which is what makes a shared information model enforceable across separately procured applications. Where shared components are financed jointly but governed separately, the pooling advantage tends to be lost to divergent specification.
